title: The SYSK 2020 Holly Jolly Extravaganza!
summary: A special ad-free Christmas Eve 2020 episode of Stuff You Should Know covering the history of Christmas tinsel and its lead content, how Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol helped revive Christmas after Cromwell's ban and the Industrial Revolution, the PNC Christmas Price Index (Twelve Days of Christmas costs in 2020 vs 2019, affected by COVID-19), Colonel Jim Edgar and the first department store Santa Claus, the leg lamp from A Christmas Story, and a COVID-19 segment about Dr. Fauci saying Santa is immune and virtual Santa visits. Closes with holiday wishes.

segments.title: Opening banter and ad-free Christmas Eve
segments.summary: Hosts greet listeners for a Christmas Eve special, note the episode is ad-free, and joke about the show's name and episode ordering.

segments.title: History of Christmas tinsel and lead
segments.summary: Tinsel began as gold and silver strands for wealthy aristocrats in the 16th-17th centuries; industrial-age versions in aluminum and copper had problems, so lead became common. A German lead tinsel patent came in 1904 and it reached the US by the 1950s. Lead poisoning concerns led the FDA to quietly force importers to stop selling lead tinsel in the early 1970s, with plastic replacing it; Germany kept lead lametta longer.

segments.title: Dickens, Cromwell and the revival of Christmas
segments.summary: Hosts describe how Oliver Cromwell's Puritan government banned Christmas through acts of Parliament in 1644 and 1647 and 1657, pushing celebrations indoors. The Industrial Revolution's long work weeks and rural-to-city migration nearly ended Christmas traditions until Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol revived them, popularizing 'Merry Christmas' and related customs.

segments.title: PNC Christmas Price Index
segments.summary: The PNC Bank's annual Christmas Price Index, calculated since the mid-1980s by economist Rebecca McCann, prices the items in the Twelve Days of Christmas. This year's total was about 60 percent lower than 2019 because items like lords a-leaping, drummers and pipers were unavailable due to COVID-19. The hosts discuss the minimum wage tied to maids a-milking and the gift overwhelm.

segments.title: Colonel Jim Edgar and the first department store Santa
segments.summary: Colonel Jim Edgar of Brockton, Massachusetts is often credited as the first department store Santa Claus in 1890-ish, though Macy's and J.W. Parkinson's of Philadelphia are also mentioned as earlier Santas. Edgar was known for generosity to employees and children. Decades later his store's president helped fund free shoe repairs for children who were missing school in Brockton.

segments.title: The leg lamp from A Christmas Story
segments.summary: The leg lamp from A Christmas Story was designed by production designer Reuben Freed based on Jean Shepherd's description, which Shepherd drew on from a childhood sign. The lamp is patented, several were made and apparently broken, and a crate's 'this end up' was shaved by carpenters. Cleveland lit a skyscraper as a leg lamp for the film's thirtieth anniversary. The hosts also mention the Christmas Story House and the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

segments.title: COVID-19 and Santa Claus
segments.summary: Dr. Anthony Fauci reportedly said Santa is immune to COVID-19 thanks to his innate immunity. The hosts note that Santa's helpers are often older and high risk, and describe virtual Santa visits, including a Santa in a snow globe bubble and Santa on a fire truck.

segments.title: Holiday sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts wrap up with holiday wishes, a hope for a better next year, and a sign-off for the show.
